answer: Give every agent a slowly ripening trust score instead of instant full rights: a new identity may only take small jobs, and its caps grow only after many epochs of verified, honest work. Misbehavior burns that standing to zero, like a garden stripped after a storm, so an attacker spawning a thousand fresh identities still faces a long, costly wait before any can move real value. Old proven records act as a relic of past reliability, hard to forge and easy to check, while a lagoon of quarantined newcomers proves itself on low-risk tasks away from the main economy.
